ui_bugs.issue: All waitlist inputs render typed text as rgb(250,250,250) on white — invisible. Verified for waitlist-business-name, waitlist-contact-name, waitlist-email, waitlist-phone, waitlist-city, waitlist-state, the GSTIN input (placeholder 22AAAAA0000A1Z5) and the message textarea. Cause: Tailwind preflight `input{color:inherit}` (0-0-1) outranks the new `:where(input...)` base rule (0-0-0), so inputs inherit body text-foreground=#fafafa in the default dark theme. Fix: revert the light-mode base rule to a plain (non-:where) `input:not(...)/select/textarea { color:#1a1918 }` and keep only the `.dark` variant inside :where(), OR add explicit `text-[#1a1918] dark:text-[#1a1918]` utilities to each waitlist input/textarea (matches what already works on the login inputs).

critical_code_review_comments: Wrapping the light-mode base input rule in :where() drops it below Tailwind preflight's `input{color:inherit}`; only the .dark override needed de-specifying. Prefer explicit per-input utilities over global base overrides for theme-mixed pages.
ThemeContext still defaults to dark on the light-themed retailer portal routes — route-scoped theming would remove this whole class of bug.

rca_of_the_issue: The :where() wrapping reduced BOTH base input rules to specificity (0,0,0). Tailwind's preflight sets `button,input,optgroup,select,textarea{...;color:inherit}` with a type-selector specificity of (0,0,1), which now wins over the :where() light-mode rule. Inputs therefore inherit the body colour, which in the default dark theme is text-foreground = #fafafa, on the light-card white input background. Inputs carrying an explicit Tailwind text utility (retailer login, specificity 0,1,0) are unaffected and render correctly.
